content: Derived sizing: Itail=60uA, I2=120uA, balance ratio=4. Candidate 1 (L=90nm) achieved Gain=623 V/V, Noise=0.026V, Current=200uA, but PM=33.8deg, SR=22.4, UGBW=24MHz. Candidate 2 tested L=45nm which achieved PM=65.6deg but collapsed Gain to 12 V/V due to ro degradation in 45nm. Lesson: Keep L>=90nm for gain. Best candidate to proceed from is Candidate 1. Levers needed: boost gm1/Cc for UGBW and tune Rc/mp3 for PM without dropping L.
Candidate 1 is best. Binding specs: ugbw (-0.612), phm (-0.279), slewRate (-0.145). Lever: scale up mn1/wn1 for gm1 boost and lower Cc to 1.2pF to attack both ugbw and slew rate, preserving L=90nm.

Candidate 4 scaled mp3=16/mp1=4 to raise gm6. Sweeping res from 1000 to 4000 ohm verified the pole-zero cancellation theory: PM scaled monotonically from 36.4deg up to 71.04deg at res=4000ohm (Candidate 11). All hard constraints except ugbw are now satisfied: Gain>700, PM=71deg, SR=32.7V/us, Noise satisfied. Only ugbw remains violated (45.4MHz vs 100MHz). Best candidate is 11 (reward -0.3523).

Candidate 11 has only ugbw violated (45.4MHz vs 100MHz). Lever: trade PM margin (71deg) and gain margin by reducing Cc from 1.2p to 0.6p, and maximizing input pair aspect ratio mn1=24, wn1=2.5u to double gm1/Cc. Re-tune Rc for 0.6pF.

Candidate 13 increased wp3=wp1=2.0u and dropped cap to 0.4pF. Swept res from 4500 to 7000 ohm: PM improved to 50.44deg and UGBW climbed to 90.71MHz at res=7000ohm (Candidate 19, reward -0.1122). Almost feasible.

Candidate 19 is near feasibility (UGBW 90.7MHz, PM 50.4deg). Lever: increase wp3=wp1=2.5u to increase gm6 (pushing p2), preserving balance ratio=4, then sweep res across 7500-9500 ohm to reach feasibility.

Reached 25 simulation budget for Phase 1. Candidate 22 (reward -0.0854, UGBW=99.2MHz, PM=48.9deg) and Candidate 23 (reward -0.0871, UGBW=102.2MHz, PM=48.4deg) are within ~10 degrees of feasibility. Handing over to Phase 3 RL refinement anchored on these near-feasible designs.

Phase 3 RL refinement completed using 700 simulations (100 warmup + 600 training). Best reward before: -0.0854; best reward after: +0.5477 (Candidate 690, fully FEASIBLE!). All constraints met: Gain=1061 V/V, PM=61.4deg, UGBW=106.6MHz, SR=38.3V/us, Noise=0.0135V, Current=203.4uA, Area=1.185e-9m^2. Key differences vs expert: cap increased to 1.6pF (PM boost), ln1=135n (Gain=1061), mn3=2/wn3=1.25u, mn4=7, mn5=6/wn5=1.25u, mp1=6, mp3=14. Handing over to Phase 2/4 optimization and polish.

Candidate 792 has FoM=0.6029. Current-class jump: increase wn3 1.25u->1.50u (+20% S_mn3) to reduce total mirrored current by ~17% (expected Itotal ~168uA). UGBW will dip below 100MHz; sizer will recover with sweep on cap and res.

Current-class jump to wn3=1.5u reduced current to 169uA but pinned UGBW at 76.6MHz due to the 2nd pole gm6/CL (CL=10pF) limit at lower I2. Increasing mn1/wn1 confirmed the circuit-analyst lesson (gm1 increase gave only +0.6% UGBW). Since recovery cannot beat Candidate 792 (FoM=0.6029), Phase 2 stops here and optimization continues from Candidate 792.

Phase 4 Polish achieved FoM=0.6259 on Candidate 910 (current=196.5uA, area=1.037e-9m^2, PM=63.1deg, UGBW=100.1MHz, Gain=1025). With 1082/2000 simulator calls used and 29 hand decisions remaining, mandatory loop triggers RL Round 2 anchored on Candidate 910.

RL Round 2 completed: 50 warmup + 400 training steps (450 sim calls used). 58 feasible designs now populated in the replay buffer. Stopped after 2 batches without improving Candidate 910 (FoM=0.6259). Handing over to Phase 4 Polish.

Opamp sizing run completed. Best design is Candidate 1723 with FoM=0.6432 (Feasible). Specifications: Gain=292.7 V/V, PM=65.86deg, UGBW=100.1MHz, SR=46.58V/us, Noise=0.00487V, Current=197.1uA, Area=0.994nm^2. Explanation written to harness_runs/harness_20261106_092530/explanation.md.
